citation: Shahhosseini M., Hu G., Huber I., Archontoulis S. V. (2021) Coupling machine learning and crop modeling improves crop yield prediction in the US Corn Belt. Scientific Reports 11, 1606. doi:10.1038/s41598-020-80820-1

dedupe_keys.name: hybrid apsim crop model and machine learning ensemble for us corn belt yield prediction

description: This model couples the process-based APSIM crop model with machine learning to predict corn yields in the US Corn Belt, feeding APSIM simulation outputs to five machine learning models, linear regression, LASSO, LightGBM, random forest and XGBoost, and to six ensembles built from them. Adding APSIM variables cut the root mean squared error of yield predictions by 7% to 20%, and soil moisture variables from APSIM proved the most influential inputs, followed by crop-related ones. It was developed by Mohsen Shahhosseini, Guiping Hu, Isaiah Huber and Sotirios Archontoulis of Iowa State University's departments of industrial and manufacturing systems engineering and agronomy, and published in Scientific Reports on 15 January 2021. Coverage is the US Corn Belt. The article is open access under CC BY 4.0; the page read does not say whether the code is shared. Caveats: it is tuned to corn in one region, and its accuracy depends on running APSIM for each site, which needs soil, weather and management data. For simulation it shows how physical crop models and statistical learners can be combined for yield forecasts under drought or heat, useful for food supply scenarios in resilience studies. It is related to the APSIM model record in this catalogue and to the interaction regression model record from the same group.
